function: p. 8: DDPG learns joint AP mode selection (information or energy APs) and per-AP downlink power allocation for SWIPT; the BD-RIS matrix uses a non-learned heuristic (p. 9).
system: p. 3, 10: cell-free massive MIMO, APs with L antennas (ML = 480), single-antenna IRs and ERs, lossless reflecting BD-RIS, fully or group-connected; frequency band not stated.
method: p. 8-9, 11: reinforcement learning, DDPG actor-critic DNNs (actor three hidden layers, critic two), off-policy, trained offline for 3,000 episodes of 500 steps, then online decisions.
data_channel: p. 3-4, 8, 10: custom simulation: Rayleigh direct links, Ricean AP-RIS link, LoS RIS-ER link, three-slope path loss with 8 dB shadowing [28]; reward from closed-form statistical-CSI expressions.
test_conditions: p. 9, 11-13: agent trained per setup (Fig. 4, M = 10 to 40); evaluated over M, Sk, receivers, pilot power; no test outside training conditions reported.
baselines: p. 9-10: non-learned only: SCA-based JAP-PA, RAP-PA (random modes, SCA power), RAP-EPA, greedy GAP-EPA; HEU vs DFT BD-RIS and D-RIS; no earlier learned method.
metrics: p. 10-13: average sum harvested energy (mW), achievable minimum SE per IR (Table III), convergence of objective and reward, execution time per iteration (Table II).
complexity: p. 8-9, 11: big-O for SCA per iteration, DDPG training and online inference, and heuristic BD-RIS design; measured runtime per iteration, ML-JAP-PA 0.038-0.047 s (Table II).
q1_support: p. 3: "A Ricean model is considered for the AP-RIS link"; p. 10: "The LSFCs are generated following the three-slope propagation model from [28]". Custom simulator (Rayleigh direct links, Ricean or LoS RIS links); no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 11: "Figure 4 illustrates the convergence of the ML-JAP-PA solution. As the network scales, the agent earns progressively higher total rewards"; p. 9: "|S| ≜ 2(M + 1) + 2(K + J) (|A| ≜ M(1 + K + J)) is the input (output) layer". The agent is trained for each setup; no test of a trained agent in a scenario or configuration not used for training is reported.
q3_support: p. 9: "A. Random AP Mode Selection and Power Control (RAP-PA)"; p. 10: "B. Random AP Mode Selection and Equal Power Allocation (RAP-EPA)", "C. Greedy AP Mode Selection and Equal Power Allocation (GAP-EPA)"; plus the SCA-based JAP-PA (p. 8). The non-learned comparison is met on sum-HE (Figs. 5-7), but there is no earlier learned method or standard learned baseline; DDPG is the proposed method itself.
q4_support: p. 9: "After the offline training, the complexity of online decision-making in the actor network is O(|S|n^µ̄ + L^µ̄(n^µ̄)^2 + n^µ̄|A|)"; p. 11, Table II: ML-JAP-PA execution time 0.0378 to 0.0472 s per iteration for M = 10 to 40.
q5_support: p. 10: "We assume that the APs and IRs are randomly distributed in a square of 0.5 × 0.5 km2". Channels are generated in the authors' own simulation; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public channel dataset.
notes: The PDF is arXiv:2507.23702v3 (19 Aug 2025); its title and authors match the Crossref record of this DOI (IEEE Trans. Commun.). Included: besides the non-learned SCA solver (JAP-PA), the paper proposes a DDPG solver (ML-JAP-PA) for the same problem (p. 8: "we propose an autonomous ML approach"). p. 13 once calls it "The ML-based benchmark", but the abstract, p. 2, Section IV-B and Figs. 5-7 present it as a proposed solution. The BD-RIS scattering matrix is set by a non-learned heuristic search (Algorithm 3, p. 9), so the RIS configuration is not learned. Area 3: the agent learns each AP's mode (PZF information precoding or PMRT energy precoding) and the power coefficients that scale the AP precoders in (21), p. 5. AP mode selection resembles association, but it is learned jointly with physical-layer power control, so above_phy does not apply. The reviewer should confirm that learned power control of the AP precoders counts as area 3. q2: training for each setup is inferred from Fig. 4 (separate training runs for M = 10 to 40), from the layer sizes that depend on M, K and J (p. 9), and from the reward, which depends on Sk (p. 12: higher Sk "greatly disturb the training process"). The paper never states that a trained agent is tested on an untrained configuration. Frequency band: footnote 1 (p. 3) gives fc = 2 GHz only as an example from [28]; the simulations do not state the carrier frequency.
